lane: H-K1-B-family adjunct experiment (geothermal-conduit blind-fault hypothesis), outside the UWBP/OCDA/CGJI lanes
experiments_note: H-GEO-CONDUIT: generate + format-validate + uniqueness-audit + holdout-diagnose one candidate; no weekly slot touched
hypothesis: Blind intrabasin faults beneath Quaternary valley fill are absent from the USGS/INGENIOUS mapped catalogue but localize upward hydrothermal flow: warm GDR springs/wells, Quaternary vents, and GeoDAWN potassium/total-count radiometric enrichment mark their concealed traces. Dots placed on this surface therefore target the off-catalogue hidden-fault class the organizer scores (known faults are masked pixel-exact), not the mapped faults in labels.tif.
mechanism: Surface = 0.35*GeoDAWN(K+TC radiometric anomaly, percentile-scaled) + 0.25*GDR well/spring temperature (90 C scale, Gaussian sigma 1.5 px) + 0.10*vent proximity (2 px dilation), slight TIGER-road edge penalty; zeroed exactly on labels.tif catalogue and outside footprint; NMS >= 2 px; binary dots capped at 37,654; official NaN-outside float32 GeoTIFF encoding.
named_non_fault_process: Felsic tuff/ash-flow contacts, playa margins, Lake Lahontan shoreline benches, and highway/road cuts can mimic radiometric or thermal anomalies; mitigated by road penalty, vent corroboration, and zeroing on mapped faults.
